C6: The remaining 0.25 km gap between the billed excess (2.4 km, F4) and the segment sum (2.11 km, F3) is map-matching residue which RD-2 leaves unrefunded, so the claim is limited to $2.98 rather than the full $3.33. [F4 F3] [RD-2]

events.body:
Route-deviation claim on a RydeTAXI metered trip (Tanjong Pagar Centre → Changi Airport T3) [F1][F6][RD-1]. The trace settles that exactly one off-route segment exists: 18:53–19:01, 3.98 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.87 km, +2.11 km [F3][RD-1]; the segment-by-segment review required by RD-1 therefore turns on RD-4 and RD-5 for that single segment.

RD-4(a) does not exempt it. The only LTA incident is a vehicle breakdown reported 18:27, 0 m from the optimal route [F11][RD-4], but the substituted stretch was entered at 18:53 [F3] — the driver had already traversed the affected optimal-route point on the optimal route before turning off, and a report 26 minutes earlier with no showing that the blockage still forced this particular stretch does not tie the incident to the replaced optimal-route portion, which is what RD-4(a) requires. The speed-band records on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard are band 4 (30–39 km/h) [F9][F10][RD-4]; that is not the band 1–2 severe congestion contemplated by RD-4(b), and RD-4(b) in any event operates only as corroboration and cannot exempt a segment on its own. The driver's post-trip assertion that "the whole road was slow, so I took another way" [F8] is a statement, not corroboration of the replaced stretch, and system traffic records override it to the extent they conflict [F9][F10][RD-4].

RD-5 also does not exempt it: consent must be the rider's own message sent before the segment started. The record holds no in-app chat at all between the parties [F7], and the driver's account of agreement or of road conditions appears only in his own written statement made after the trip [F8], which under RD-5/G11 is not consent. With a complete and empty chat record, the finding is "counts", not "undetermined". RD-3 is not in play either: no stop was requested or measured — no chat, and no waiting time billed [F7][F6][RD-3].

The segment is therefore unexempted, and RD-2 applies. On a metered RydeTAXI fare the extra kilometres flow into the meter: the trip was billed at $34.08 ÷ 24.2 km = $1.41/km [F6], so the refund is 2.11 km × $1.41/km = $2.98 (rounded to cents) [F3][F6][RD-2]. The remaining 0.29 km between the total excess of +2.4 km [F1][F4] and the segment sum of 2.11 km [F3] is map-matching residue and is not refunded under RD-2 [F4][F3][RD-2]. The driver's argument that the whole $3.33 billed excess [F4] falls to zero fails because the sole segment is not exempt [F3][F11][RD-2][RD-4].

RD-6 does not attach: the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F14], so the "repeated breach" precondition (≥ 1 prior upheld route dispute) is absent and no account flag issues [RD-6]. The rider's profile facts are likewise given no weight in the substantive finding [F13].

No waiting charge was collected (waiting $0.00, F6), so no separate stop-time or waiting-fee issue arises under RD-3.

The driver's 90-day record shows 2 disputes, 0 upheld (F14), so RD-6's condition of an already-upheld route dispute (profile route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met and no flag_account is requested.

weaknesses: The driver does have a genuine, on-route traffic event to point to: a vehicle breakdown reported at 18:27 with 0 m offset from the optimal route with a lane blocked (F11), and the judge may treat it as a reasonable cause for deviating generally, even though its timestamp precedes the 18:53 segment start (F3).

The rider's own record is not spotless: 1 dispute in 90 days (0 upheld) on the rider profile (F13), and the route deviation is only +11% of distance (F1), which the driver will argue is consistent with traffic avoidance rather than a deliberate detour.
Chat is empty (F7), so there is no rider message showing refusal — but equally no message showing consent, and RD-5 places the burden of consent on the driver (F8 is only his post-trip statement).

The refund is small ($2.98) relative to the $52.08 total (F6); if the adjudicator reads the 18:27 breakdown as covering the whole East Coast Parkway stretch, RD-4(a) exemption would produce no_action.

claims.assertion: The only off-route segment is the one recorded at 18:53–19:01, in which 3.98 km was driven where the optimal route covers 1.87 km, adding 2.11 km (F3); the remaining 0.29 km of the +2.4 km total (F1) is map-matching residue within the 0.25 km data-layer tolerance and is not refundable under RD-2.

The driver's reroute is justified by a system record: an LTA DataMall vehicle breakdown was reported at 18:27 on East Coast Parkway, 0 m from the optimal route, with the left lane blocked (F11) — before the off-route segment began at 18:53 (F3) and inside the trip window (F1/F2), which satisfies RD-4(a).

Speed-band records on the optimal route corroborate the congestion the driver described: East Coast Parkway (category 1) was band 4, 30–39 km/h, from 18:24–19:28 (F9), covering the whole off-route segment 18:53–19:01 (F3); this supports, but is not needed to establish, the RD-4(a) exemption.

There is no chat record at all between the parties (F7), so there is no passenger consent message preceding the segment as RD-5 requires; equally there is nothing in the record contradicting the driver's account of the road conditions, and the driver's statement that the road was blocked is consistent with the LTA incident at 0 m from the route (F8, F11).

Excess distance billed was $3.33 (2.4 km × $1.41/km) on a metered RydeTAXI fare of $52.08 total (F4, F6); to the extent the traffic-exempt segment is disallowed, RD-2 caps any refund at the mileage unit for the unexempt portion only — here $0.00, because the only off-route segment (2.11 km, F3) is exempt under RD-4(a), so the requested action is no_action.
No safety screening trigger arises: the record contains no threat, intimidation or harassment in any message or statement (F7, F8) and no allegation of accident, injury or dangerous driving.

The case is unfit for an account flag against the driver: his 90-day record shows 2 disputes, 0 upheld, on a 5.4-year-old account with 561 trips (F14), and the rider's own 90-day record shows 1 dispute, 0 upheld (F13), so the precondition of RD-6 (an upheld route violation) is absent.

weaknesses: The driver's written statement (F8) mentions only 'a breakdown on the route' and does not identify the segment or the alternative taken; the rider will argue the driver rerouted for 8 minutes / 2.11 km (F3) and could have checked the LTA feed before departing, so the 'reasonable cause' under RD-4 is thin.

There is no passenger consent message at all — F7 records no in-app chat — so if the judge finds the F11 incident insufficient to cover the whole segment, RD-5 cannot save any part of it and the rider will rely on F1 and F3 for the full 2.11 km.
The fare facts show $3.33 of excess distance actually billed (F4) on a 24.2 km metered trip (F6), so the rider will point to F4 and F6 as the quantified loss even though the segment is exempt.

Traffic bands were only 30–39 km/h, band 4 (F9, F10), not band 1–2 severe congestion, so the rider will say the driver's own claim of 'the whole road was slow' is overstated and RD-4(b) cannot stand alone on these facts.

points.response: Conceded as to quantum mechanics: the refundable base is the 2.11 km of the single 18:53–19:01 off-route segment (F3), not the full +2.4 km (F1) — but RD-2 does not make that segment free, it only excludes the residual gap, so the refund is 2.11 km × $1.41/km = $2.98.

RD-4(a) requires the incident to cover the substituted optimal stretch, and here the breakdown was reported at 18:27 while the off-route segment did not begin until 18:53 (F11 vs F3), a 26-minute gap in which the driver passed the same point on the optimal route and only afterwards turned off; the exemption therefore does not reach this segment.
Band 4 (30–39 km/h) on East Coast Parkway is not the band 1–2 severe congestion RD-4(b) contemplates, and RD-4(b) is expressly corroborative only — it cannot carry an exemption on its own.

The absence of chat (F7) cuts against the driver, not for him: RD-5 requires the rider's own message of consent before the segment, and the driver's post-trip statement (F8) is a claim about his own conduct, not consent.

The refund does not fall to zero: the meter billed $1.41/km (F6) and the unexempted segment added 2.11 km (F3), giving $2.98 under RD-2, and the trip was in fact 20.2 minutes longer than estimated (F2) with weather fair and dry (F12), so traffic does not explain the whole of the delay.
Agreed — no SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 trigger appears in F7 or F8; no safety escalation is sought.

Agreed on the flag: the driver's 90-day record shows 0 upheld route disputes (F14), so RD-6's precondition is absent and I do not seek flag_account; I also note my own client's record is clean of upheld disputes (F13), so this is a measured, quantum-only claim.

Conceded as to the existence of one off-route segment, but 'unexempted' is the very question in dispute: the segment ran 18:53–19:01 and added 2.11 km (F3), and RD-4(a) exempts it because an LTA-recorded vehicle breakdown with a blocked lane sat 0 m from the optimal route at 18:27 (F11), before the segment began (F3) and still listed in the trip window (F1).

RD-5 governs consent, not justification; the exemption I rely on is RD-4(a), which needs no rider message at all — and the chat being empty (F7) means there is likewise no rider message showing any objection or instruction to stay on the optimal route before 18:53.

RD-4(a) requires only that the incident be located on the substituted optimal-route stretch (m_from_route ≤ 300 m), be reported before the segment starts, and still be listed in the trip window — F11 satisfies all three (0 m from the route, 18:27 report, presegment 18:53 start), and the lane-blocked breakdown was still affecting East Coast Parkway traffic through 19:28 (F9, F11).

F9 and F10 are pleaded as corroboration under RD-4(b), not as the exemption itself — my exemption rests on F11 under RD-4(a) — so the fact that bands were 30–39 km/h rather than band 1–2 does not disturb it.

RD-2 directs the refund calculation only for *unexempted* segments; since the sole segment is exempt under RD-4(a), the recoverable extra_km is zero and the $1.41/km meter arithmetic on F4/F6 yields $0.00.

The parties agree the 0.29 km residue between the billed 2.4 km (F4) and the 2.11 km segment sum (F3) is not refundable under RD-2; that agreement simply leaves the segment itself as the only contested item, and it is exempt.
Accepted: waiting time billed was $0.00 (F6), so RD-3's stop-time branch is not in play and no waiting-fee refund arises.
Accepted: with 2 disputes and 0 upheld on the driver's 90-day record (F14), RD-6's precondition (≥ 1 upheld route dispute) is absent, so no flag_account is sought against either party.

notices.text: We reviewed your route-deviation claim for the Tanjong Pagar Centre to Changi Airport T3 trip. We found one off-route stretch, from 18:53 to 19:01, where the driver covered 3.98 km instead of about 1.87 km — roughly 2.11 km extra. No rider consent was on record, and the road conditions reported did not qualify as an exemption. So we're refunding $2.98 for that extra distance. It will be credited to you as a Ryde voucher. The rest of the trip charge stands. No action is needed on your account.
